title: We built a self-improving macro thesis engine that forecasts what the market hasn't priced in yet.
author: Depth4dotcom
selftext:
By the time a chart moves, the move is mostly over. DEPTH4 maps the chain of consequences *before* the price reacts, surfacing live, tradeable SIGNALS across equities, rates, FX, and commodities.

Its core differentiator is "*Blind Spot*"—a mathematically verified metric showing exactly how much of a macro move the market has yet to price in. Instead of relying on AI guesswork, DEPTH4 calculates this blind spot using real Wall Street options data and realized volatility. If the market is underpricing a catalyst, DEPTH4 flags it.

Unlike static AI tools, DEPTH4 is built on a self-calibrating, three-layer memory architecture:

\*   **It knows its own edge:** Before writing a thesis, the engine checks its 90-day historical win rate for the specific macro mechanism it is trading (e.g., "CTA trend unwinding") and hard-clamps its own conviction based on its actual track record. 

\*   **It remembers:** It uses retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) to review its past successful and failed theses for that exact setup, learning from structural mistakes before generating a new trade plan.

\*   **It evolves its playbook:** Every week, the AI reviews its worst trades, proposes new rules to prevent repeating mistakes, tests them against a historical regression suite, and injects the approved rules into its own brain for all future generations.

The output is the *SIGNALS page*—a live dashboard that rolls up all active theses on an asset into one clear card showing direction (Long/Short/Mixed), signal strength, and unpriced Room. Every signal is fully drillable, meaning users never face a "black box" prediction. They can see the exact D1–D4 causal chain, the underlying evidence timeline, and the mathematical reasoning behind the edge.

DEPTH4 doesn't just tell you what happened. It proves *why* an asset is about to move, calculates *how much* is left to gain, and continuously sharpens its own intelligence over time.

replies.author: Depth4dotcom
replies.body:
Hey — thanks for registering, really appreciate it.

Great question. DEPTH4 isn’t a fixed-rule trading bot, so it’s not backtestable in the classic “here’s an EA, run it on 10 years of M15 data” way.

What it *is*: a macro intelligence engine that reads news, traces how stories cascade through markets (D1→D4), and surfaces SIGNALS — direction, strength, and how much room is left before the market has priced it in.

On validation: yes, we’ve built that in. Every signal that passes our tradability filter gets scored against real price data at 7, 14, and 30-day horizons. We also run a trader simulation — enter when the signal is highly actionable and price agrees; exit when conviction drops, room tightens, or direction goes mixed.

That history is still accumulating (we’re early), so sample size is growing week by week. We use it internally to gate what we surface — we’d rather show fewer signals that hold up than flood you with headline noise.

If you want, I can share how we think about measuring edge vs. just being directionally right.

replies.author: Depth4dotcom
replies.body:
This is exactly the kind of setup we had in mind, and thank you for signing up.

Your stack (research agents → trading → execution) maps cleanly to how we're building DEPTH4: signals for the daily read, full thesis cascades when you need depth, and soon MCP so your LangChain/Claude agents can pull both without scraping the UI.

What's live today while you're exploring:

* SIGNALS -- daily actionable view: direction, room, tradability
* Theses -- full D1–D4 cascades, cause chains, trade context
* Feed -- what changed as new evidence hits open theses
* Book -- link positions to theses and see conflicts / alignment (Pro)
* Star assets or theses you care about -- the engine tracks shifts on those names

What you're describing — and yes, we're building toward it:

* Daily signal digest + deeper thesis reports on demand
* Portfolio- and industry-aware updates ("tell me what matters to *my* book")
* MCP tools your agents can call: `list_actionable_signals`, `get_thesis`, `get_feed_since`, copilot-style context per symbol

Industry focus is a sweet spot for us: the cascade logic (D1 headline → D2 reaction → D3 spillover → D4 regime) is built for sector-level reasoning, not generic market summaries.

I've got you on the list for early MCP access. In the meantime: star your sector names, add anything you're holding to Book, and tell me which industries you care about most -- that helps us prioritize what lands in v1.

Will keep you posted. Appreciate you reaching out.

comments.body: Is it ironic that it looks like a divining rod and plate?  On a serious note am i understanding that it's just reinforcement learning in real time.  Do you have multiple instances running that compare to one another?  I'd like to see an A/B test of a couple models moving in half step with one-another.

replies.author: Depth4dotcom
replies.body:
Divining rod, hah — unintentional but I'll own it. Under the hood it's causal macro reasoning, not mysticism.

Not RL: no live training on rewards. News → thesis cascades → evidence updates → signal roll-up, with hard quality gates.

No parallel A/B instances running today — one pipeline, tiered models paired with crowd intelligence, , escalate on failure.
